What Is Olatorepatide?

Olatorepatide (HS-20094) is an investigational once-weekly injectable dual-biased GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonist developed by Hansoh Pharmaceutical (China). MW ~5020 Da, formula C235H357N49O72. Phase 3 LIGHTEN results presented at EASD 2026 showed up to 19.3% weight loss at 48 weeks. China NMPA accepted the NDA in June 2026; Regeneron licensed global rights in December 2025.

Mechanism of Action

  • GLP-1 receptor activation: Suppresses appetite, slows gastric emptying, enhances insulin secretion.
  • GIP receptor activation: Enhances insulin sensitivity, may attenuate GLP-1-associated nausea.
  • Biased agonism: Selective downstream signaling pathway engagement — potentially reduces side effects while preserving efficacy vs non-biased dual agonists.

Key Research Findings

Phase 3 LIGHTEN (EASD 2026)

  • Olatorepatide 15 mg: −19.3% weight loss at 48 weeks (efficacy estimand) vs −2.5% placebo
  • Treatment-regimen estimand: −11.8% / −17.0% / −18.7% for 5/10/15 mg
  • Zero early discontinuations due to drug-related adverse events
  • 604 participants randomized 1:1:1:1

Regulatory Milestones

  • December 2025: Regeneron licenses ex-Greater China global rights
  • June 2026: China NMPA accepts NDA for obesity indication
  • Global Phase 3 under Regeneron planned

Dosing in Research

Phase 3 doses: 5 mg, 10 mg, 15 mg weekly subcutaneous. Investigational only; not approved anywhere as of October 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does dual-biased mean?

Selective activation of specific downstream pathways within both GLP-1 and GIP receptors. May attenuate nausea while preserving weight-loss efficacy. Phase 3 showed favorable tolerability with zero drug-related early discontinuations.

How does olatorepatide compare to tirzepatide?

Both target GLP-1 and GIP receptors. LIGHTEN reported −19.3% at 48 weeks; SURMOUNT-1 showed −20.9% at 72 weeks. No head-to-head trial. Biased agonism significance unproven in comparative trials.

What is olatorepatide's regulatory status?

China NMPA NDA accepted June 2026 (review ongoing). Not approved in US or Europe. Regeneron global Phase 3 planned. Research compounds discussed for educational purposes. Consult a healthcare provider before use.

Research Limitations

  • LIGHTEN data from company press release only; no peer-reviewed publication as of October 2026
  • Chinese population only; global Phase 3 pending
  • No head-to-head vs tirzepatide or semaglutide
  • Biased agonism clinical significance unproven
  • Not approved anywhere as of October 2026
